data.title: AI is driving a flood of crypto bug reports. Now it’s helping sort them
data.description:
Crypto bug bounty platforms have expanded their use of artificial intelligence to keep up with a growing mountain of AI-assisted security reports.

Crypto-focused HackenProof said in October that it was using AI to triage 70% of submissions fully autonomously, aiming to hit 85% by the end of 2026. It said it received an average of about 6,100 bug reports a month in the third quarter, 2.4 times the reports from December last year.

Rival Immunefi last week said submissions to its platform rose 136% year-over-year in the first nine months of 2026, as it introduced a tool that can flag duplicates before a researcher submits a report.

Bug bounty programs pay independent researchers to find and report potential security flaws. AI has helped researchers uncover more genuine vulnerabilities, but has also swelled the volume of invalid and duplicate submissions, making it harder for security teams to identify the threats that need urgent attention.

It’s like “bringing a sword to a gunfight,” Dmitry Tokarev, founder of crypto wallet provider Bron, told Cointelegraph, referring to security teams that haven’t already adopted AI to sift through reports.

The turning point for AI-assisted bug hunting

Several bug bounty platforms have identified February as a turning point in the surge of AI-assisted vulnerability reports, coinciding with the release of more capable AI models, including Anthropic’s Claude Opus 4.6.

HackenProof said Claude Opus 4.6 could work through larger codebases and sustain tasks for longer. HackerOne said the arrival of more capable AI models and tools in that month saw a sudden shift from a “human-only submission environment.”

Graph showing HackenProof's volume of bug reports per month. Source: HackenProof

Some crypto developers are also experimenting with financial disincentives to curb low-quality submissions.

The team behind Firedancer, a Solana validator client developed by Jump Crypto, which also uses AI to screen reports, took an additional measure in October.

To deter spam, it began requiring researchers to burn 1 SOL for each bug report they want considered for a bounty. The token is permanently destroyed, even if the report turns out to be a duplicate.

In a November update published Tuesday, HackerOne’s vice president of operations Tony Lee said they began requiring researchers to verify their identities before submitting reports in the third quarter. It also expanded its triage team and began using AI agents to automatically close clear-cut cases, such as spam and duplicate reports.

In October, it gave customers more control over how many reports their public programs receive.

Security teams brace for more bug reports and attacks

Lee said he expects vulnerability reports to keep climbing “for the foreseeable future” after recording a 22% increase in report volume in Q3 compared to the previous quarter.

Meanwhile, insurer QBE and risk consultancy Control Risks on Wednesday forecast more disruptive cyber incidents in 2027 across the 14 markets they studied, pointing to the “industrialization of AI” as one of the factors.

Mike Blank, chief product officer at blockchain infrastructure firm R3, also said he expects the number of hacks to rise sharply in 2027, but said crypto teams should pay closer attention to how much damage a single breach can cause, rather than the number of attacks.

“The real difference will be between protocols where a stolen key can drain everything and those where it can only pause operations,” Blank said.

data.title: Commodity Corner: Oil set for first weekly gain this month; gold steadies
data.description:
Commodity markets traded mixed on November 27, with oil prices heading for their first weekly gain this month amid concerns over Middle East supply disruptions, while gold prices steadied as investors weighed interest-rate expectations against a recovery in global markets.

Oil was on track for the first weekly gain this month as attacks on energy infrastructure and tankers in the Middle East raised concerns escalating hostilities could disrupt exports.

Brent traded near $97 a barrel and was up 4.5% this week, while West Texas Intermediate was around $85

Gold steadied, as traders weighed the prospect of Federal Reserve interest-rate hikes against a wider market recovery spurred by a rebound in US technology stocks.

Bullion was near $3,565 an ounce, on track for a modest weekly gain after sinking to a 15-month low earlier in a week of

choppy trading.

The US dollar hovered below a 22-month peak in holiday-thinned trading on Friday, with traders looking to equity markets for clues on direction as doubts about the AI trade triggers heightened volatility.

The dollar index, which measures the currency against a basket of six peers, was steady at 103.81, at the end of a week that saw it pop to the highest level since March of last year at 104.53 on Monday only to erase those gains a day later. For the week, the index is currently flat.

The US currency edged up 0.1% to 159.355 yen early in Friday's Asian session, and also strengthened slightly to 0.83455 Swiss franc.

The euro was little changed at $1.0964 and sterling eased slightly to $1.3099.

data.title: Venezuela signs Siemens Energy deals to fix power grid
data.description:
Venezuela signed agreements with Germany's Siemens Energy in Caracas to repair and upgrade the national electricity network and the power infrastructure that serves its oil sector, Telesur reported.

Acting President Delcy Rodriguez said sanctions had prevented the grid from obtaining Siemens parts and equipment for more than 10 years.

After ten years of recurring power cuts, the government is pursuing these agreements to bring them to an end, and officials attribute the outages to a blockade led by the United States. According to the authorities, that blockade has deprived the electrical network and the oil sector alike of replacement components, technical know-how and funding.

Rodriguez tied the accords to the Venezuela Rises Plan, a development programme unveiled one day ahead of the signing, whose goals are economic stabilisation, faster growth and resolution of the national debt. Reliable power, she argued, is the foundation for attracting new investment and bringing production back.

'Venezuela’s electrical system was unable to access parts and equipment for more than a decade. In the specific case of Siemens, we could not access because of the issue of sanctions and now we are making it possible,' Rodriguez said.

Under the agreements, in which the Ministry of People's Power for Electric Energy also participated, power plants are to run more effectively and the oil sector is to make better use of its gas while meeting environmental sustainability standards. The report says that gas currently burned off or not fully exploited might instead be channelled into electricity generation, cutting waste and relieving pressure on the national grid.

Rodriguez said the bilateral deal would accelerate repairs because the electricity ministry and state oil company PDVSA had already identified exactly which components need replacing. Siemens has operated in Venezuela for over 70 years and supports a large share of its thermoelectric capacity.

Rodriguez expressed gratitude to Christian Bruch, chief executive of Siemens Energy, and to the delegation of German companies that travelled to Caracas. She gave credit to Germany's ambassador, whose diplomatic work, started two years ago, cleared the path for shared projects once more. She further remembered that after twin earthquakes hit parts of Venezuela in June, Germany dispatched rescue teams and humanitarian aid.

No timeline for the work was announced. Rodriguez ordered technical teams from state power utility Corpoelec, PDVSA and Siemens Energy to begin operations immediately.

data.title: Tokyo's core CPI hits 2.9%, strengthening case for BOJ rate hike in December
data.description:
Tokyo's consumer prices rose at their fastest pace this year in November, strengthening the case for the Bank of Japan (BOJ) to raise interest rates next month as it works to keep inflation near its 2% target.

Core consumer price index (CPI) in the capital, which leaves out volatile fresh food, climbed 2.9% from a year earlier, the highest since July 2025, the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications said on Friday, with the overall CPI rising 2.8%.

Tokyo's figures act as an early signal for the national picture, so the result gave the central bank fresh evidence that prices were still climbing. The measure that strips out both fresh food and energy, which the BOJ watches closely as a guide to underlying inflation, rose 2.5%.

Higher utility bills drove much of the increase, as electricity costs rose 9.5% and city gas bills climbed almost 14%, the ministry said, as summer subsidies introduced by Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's government came to an end. Processed food prices also rose slightly faster.

Rice offered some relief as its price fell almost 34%, the steepest drop in records dating back to 1971, after it had been a main force behind inflation a year earlier.

The data also fitted with the BOJ's recent stance, as last month, the bank judged that underlying inflation had reached a level broadly in line with its 2% goal, and it shifted its focus from pushing prices higher to keeping them steady around that level.

Government policy has however seemed to make that judgement harder as Takaichi announced last month that utility subsidies would return for three months from December, and she wants to cut the sales tax on food from April. The government also plans to scale back gasoline subsidies.

Earlier this week, the BOJ's own gauge, which removes the effect of temporary government measures, rose to 3.5% in October, its fastest in three years. Prices that businesses charge each other for services rose by the most in 36 years.

Companies have passed on higher costs linked to the West Asia conflict far more readily than in the era of long deflation and Teikoku Databank said major food and drink makers planned to raise prices on 1,477 products this month, almost ten times the number a year earlier.

Households have seemed to be the main affected with real wages, which are pay adjusted for inflation, having risen every month this year, yet consumer spending shrank for two straight quarters to September, and the government downgraded its view of consumption this week.

Governor Kazuo Ueda had said the bank would weigh the economy, inflation and financial conditions when deciding when to move. He is due to give a speech on Monday, and the BOJ announces its next rate decision on December 18.

data.title: Brent trades near month's high as Mideast conflict threatens supply
data.description:
Key points:
  • Attack on Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery halts some operations
  • OPEC+ likely to roll over oil output targets for Q1
  • Russian oil refinery in Krasnodar region on fire after drone attack

By Florence Tan

Brent crude futures hovered near this month's high on Friday as ongoing attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi energy infrastructure heightened concerns over oil exports from the conflict-hit region.

Brent crude futures fell 38 cents, or 0.39%, to $96.19 a barrel by 0140 GMT, after gaining nearly $2 on Thursday to settle at their highest since November 6.

US West Texas Intermediate crude futures were at $85.41 a barrel, up $1.73, or 2.07%, from their close on Wednesday. There was no settlement for WTI on Thursday due to the Thanksgiving holiday.

"We think Brent can still push above USD100/bbl without another major escalation in the Middle East, but that increasingly requires evidence of constrained deliverable supply," ANZ analysts Brian Martin and Daniel Hynes said in a note.

Both benchmarks are headed for their first weekly gain in four weeks. Prices slipped in previous weeks on relief that US President Donald Trump did not step up military action on Iran after the US midterm elections.

However, Iran has continued to attack ships transiting the Hormuz strait, disrupting oil exports, while Iran-aligned Yemeni Houthis have targeted Saudi energy infrastructure and ports.

Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery temporarily halted some operations after a projectile struck the facility on Thursday, killing a Nepalese worker and wounding several others, Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry said in a statement.

The strike was the Houthis' latest blow against key Saudi facilities, a day after the group claimed attacks on Ras Tanura, the kingdom's largest refinery and a major crude export hub, and the Red Sea ports of Jeddah and Jazan, amid escalating hostilities between the two sides.

Given the disruption from the Iran war, OPEC+ is likely to maintain its oil output targets for at least the first quarter of 2027 at a meeting on Sunday, two people with knowledge of the talks said.

Meanwhile, Ukraine has intensified drone attacks on Russian oil refineries since the end of October with the latest incident causing a fire at the Slavyansk ECO refinery in Russia's southern Krasnodar region. These attacks have hit Russia's refining output and fuel exports, tightening global diesel supplies.

Fires also hit Thailand's Bangchak refinery and Venezuela's Amuay refinery on Thursday.

Separately, an incident at the Bacalhau oilfield offshore Brazil has halted production for an estimated five to eight weeks, both the operator, Equinor , and its partner, Galp , said on Wednesday.

data.title: Philippines' trade deficit widens to a record $6.9 billion in October
data.description:
The Philippines posted its widest trade deficit on record in October, government data showed on Friday, with both exports and imports growing at the highest rate in more than five years.

  • Exports (PHEXP=ECI) rose 41.8% and imports (PHIMP=ECI) grew 50.4% on an annual basis, the Philippine Statistics Authority said, the most since April 2021

  • The value of the exports reached $10.57 billion and imports hit $17.52 billion, both the highest since record began in 1991, with the trade deficit widening to an all-time high of $6.95 billion (PHTBAL=ECI)

  • The United States was the Philippines’ biggest export market in October, taking $2.76 billion, or 26.1% of total shipments, while China remained its largest source of imports at $5.19 billion, or 29.6% of the total

  • For the first 10 months of 2026, the value of exports rose 20.1% to a record $84.71 billion, while imports increased 23.9% to a record $139.09 billion

data.title: China's industrial firms post faster profit growth as recovery remains uneven
data.description:
Profit growth at China's industrial firms accelerated in October, supported by improving conditions in parts of the manufacturing sector, although broader economic momentum remained subdued.

With domestic demand yet to gain meaningful traction and continuing to weigh on corporate earnings, many firms have increasingly relied on overseas markets for growth, leaving them vulnerable to trade tensions and geopolitical risks.

Profits at industrial firms rose 20.1% from a year earlier last month, versus a 14.4% gain in September, data from the National Bureau of Statistics showed on Friday. Profits were up 16% in the first 10 months, accelerating from a 15.5% increase in the January-September period,

Industrial earnings continued to show a sharp split, with profits in computer, telecommunications and other electronic equipment manufacturing doubling in the first 10 months, while furniture manufacturing posted a decline of 52.4%.

The uneven performance comes as Beijing has introduced a series of policy measures in recent months aimed at supporting economic activity, including steps to lower borrowing costs, increase liquidity in the financial system and channel financing to sectors such as technology, manufacturing and infrastructure.

Still, analysts say the impact of the policy support has been mixed, with weak household demand and lingering strains in the property sector continuing to drag on the broader recovery.

The outlook for exports, a key source of support for manufacturers this year, has meanwhile become less certain. Concerns over potential tariff increases and other trade restrictions, particularly in the United States and the European Union, have raised questions about the sustainability of export-driven growth and the earnings prospects of firms dependent on overseas demand.

Industrial profit figures cover firms with annual revenue of at least 20 million yuan ($3 million) from main operations.

($1 = 6.6722 Chinese yuan)

data.title: New Zealand’s ruling coalition falls just short of majority in final election count
data.description:
New Zealand’s ruling centre-right coalition has narrowly missed winning a parliamentary majority, final election results showed on Friday, leaving Prime Minister Christopher Luxon needing the support of the centrist Opportunity Party to remain in power.

Data from the Electoral Commission showed the coalition with 65 seats, one seat short of a majority in the 130-seat parliament.

Luxon’s centre-right National Party secured 40 seats in the November 7 election, and its junior coalition partners Act and New Zealand First won 13 seats and 12 seats, respectively.

Labour, the largest opposition party, won 36 seats.

New political party Opportunity won seven seats. Opportunity leader Qiulae Wong has said she would negotiate first with the party that won the most seats.

The results show a centre-left coalition of Labour, the Green Party and Te Pati Maori would not be able to form a government, even with the support of Opportunity.

The New Zealand dollar , which hit a 17-year low against the US dollar this week, strengthened slightly after the announcement of the election results.

Earlier this month, preliminary results from the Electoral Commission had shown the ruling coalition with a majority of two seats. The final tally includes special votes, which include those from people voting overseas or outside their electorate, and typically skew left.

The Electoral Commission said there were 2,931,604 votes cast, of which 484,865 were special votes.

data.title: BOJ calls for safeguards against digital money, AI risks
data.description:
By Leika Kihara

Global policymakers must strengthen defences against financial stability and cybersecurity risks posed by the emergence of new forms of digital money and financial infrastructure, Bank of Japan Executive Director Kazushige Kamiyama said on Friday.

New forms of digital money, such as stablecoins and tokenised deposits, are likely to co-exist and interact, which poses fresh challenges for policymakers such as ensuring the diversity does not create unnecessary fragmentation or undermine financial stability, he said.

The growing use of AI also brings fresh cybersecurity risks, requiring authorities and institutions to strengthen their defences against the growing ability of AI to discover and exploit vulnerabilities, Kamiyama said.

"My central message is that technological innovation offers significant opportunities to improve money and payments, but innovation must go hand in hand with trust," Kamiyama said in a speech delivered to the International Monetary Fund's seminar on digital money and payments in Tokyo.

"Central bank money will continue to play a fundamental role as the anchor of trust in the monetary system," he said.

data.title: MISSION SUCCESS: Rocket Lab Launches 101st Electron Mission
data.description:
MAHIA, New Zealand, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Rocket Lab Corporation , a global leader in launch services and space systems, today successfully completed another dedicated Electron launch for synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite operator Synspective.

The ‘Night Owls Never Sleep’ mission launched from Rocket Lab Launch Complex 1 in New Zealand at 1:15 p.m. NZDT on 27 September 2026, delivering the 14h StriX satellite directly into a 569km low Earth orbit. This latest addition further scales Synspective’s Earth-observation constellation that gathers high-resolution images of the planet's surface regardless of weather conditions or time of day.

Today’s mission was Rocket Lab’s 22nd launch of 2026 and 101st mission overall, extending Electron’s lead as the world’s most frequently-launched small-lift orbital rocket.

Mission Highlights:

  • Unmatched Track Record: Maintaining a 100% mission success rate for Synspective, Rocket Lab has been the sole launch provider for all 14 StriX satellites to date.
  • Rapid Constellation Building: As Rocket Lab’s 22nd mission of the year, today’s launch highlights Electron’s high-cadence reliability that commercial constellation operators depend on to scale their operations on schedule.
  • Record-Breaking Partnership: Following a historic 20-launch deal signed in September - the largest commercial contract for Electron to date - Synspective is Rocket Lab’s largest launch customer with 47 total missions booked. Today’s launch leaves 33 dedicated missions on the manifest to be launched through 2031, giving Synspective long-term certainty as they build out their constellation.

data.title: Japan eyeing $350 billion five-year defence plan, below military's wishes, Asahi reports
data.description:
Japan's government is considering setting defence spending at 56.3 trillion yen ($353 billion) over the five years from fiscal 2027, below the levels sought by defence officials, the Asahi newspaper reported.

Asked about the report, Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said on Friday that spending should be determined by Japan's defence needs rather than a pre-set numerical target.

"Rather than starting with a specific spending figure, what matters is determining concretely and realistically what is needed," Katayama said in a regular news conference.

The reported budget figure falls within the range between 50 trillion and 60 trillion yen that Finance Ministry officials have proposed for defence over the five years starting in April 2027.

While more than the 43 trillion yen allocation in the current five-year plan, it falls well short of the 80 trillion yen ​budget that some defence officials and ruling Liberal Democratic Party lawmakers had assumed and used in negotiations with contractors.

It would also leave Japan short ​of its target of raising defence outlays to 2% of gross domestic product, according to Reuters calculations.

Asahi, citing multiple government sources, said Tokyo plans to brief the United States on its latest thinking. Washington has urged allies, including Japan, to raise defence spending to 3.5% of GDP.

The final amount could still be adjusted higher, the newspaper said.

The government plans to revise its national security strategy and related defence documents by year-end.
